chapter.title: Temporary Power
chapter.sub: Every morning at seven, a temporary breaker trips. The racks are on it — and so is the lighting preheat.

items.text: SEASON 8 · EPISODE 2 · DRAFT · CASE-041  Seven o’clock trips · Maya, Tove, Bram and Kit · Level L5 · Advanced support (formulas on request)  Every morning at seven, a temporary breaker trips. The AV racks are on it. So is the lighting preheat. Neither was in the electrician’s plan.  ⚑ RV-160: temporary and permanent power are the electrician’s; Maya resets nothing and plugs nothing in. RV-161: figures illustrative. Some choices run on a clock.

items.title: Temporary Power
items.stakes: A temporary breaker trips at seven every morning. Your racks are on it — and so is the lighting preheat.
items.clock: Before the two-week burn-in window closes.
items.reward: Seven quiet mornings, and an electrician who knows every load on her panel.

objectives.text: Decide what to do about the trip
Decide where the racks get power
Decide how trades ask for power

items.alt: The hall floor at 7:05 a.m.: a temporary distribution panel with one breaker handle shown red; Tove, the electrician's foreman, points at it; Maya stands back.

bubbles.text: Then tell me what's on it.

items.caption: The same breaker, the same minute, six days running.

lines.text: Then tell me what's on it — and I'll tell you everything of ours that should be.

items.prompt: 07:10. The AV contractor wants T3 reset so burn-in can restart. What do you do?
known: ◉ Racks A and B on T3
items.risk: Burn-in lost daily — or someone working on a panel that isn't theirs.
timeout: The AV contractor resets it while you're on the phone.

hints.text: Whose panel is it — and what does she need from you?

options.label: Reset the breaker yourself
options.result: Tove: “My panel. Nobody resets until I know why.”

options.label: Ask Tove what's on T3, and meanwhile write down every AV load — watts and hours — for her
options.result: Racks A and B, and the lighting group that comes on at seven. Your schedule shows 3,600 W of AV running around the clock.
options.consequence: Ask the owner; give her numbers.

options.label: Unplug the lighting washes
options.result: The lighting contractor's preheat is part of their fixture warranty routine.

options.label: Tell the AV contractor to plug into whatever circuit is free
options.result: The trip moves to T4 on Thursday.
options.consequence: An unplanned load on an unplanned circuit.

items.title: Seven o'clock.
items.body: The lighting contractor's console runs a preheat at 07:00: twelve LED washes on at once, on T3 — where racks A and B were already drawing 16.7 A, over the 16 A planning line. The washes add 9.6 A running, and switched together their drivers surge to something like 192 A for a few milliseconds. The breaker does exactly its job.
items.label: Test: how much current — and why seven?

items.alt: Temporary panel TP-2 as found: T1 11.7 A, T2 6.7 A, T3 in red at 26.3 A with racks A and B and twelve washes at 07:00, T4 empty; the 16 A planning line dashed; below: 07:00 preheat, surge about 192 A, trip.
items.caption: Two plans nobody shared.

items.sub: Advanced · the skill behind this chapter

items.alt: A teaching moment: Tove and Maya beside a board. Twelve LED washes at eight-tenths of an amp each. Switched on together, each driver surges to twenty times that for a few milliseconds. Running, nine point six amps. For those milliseconds, nearer two hundred — well into the breaker's instant-trip range. So I stagger them in three groups. My circuits, my sequence. You tell me what your racks draw.

items.caption: Advanced: the formula is there if you ask. Try without it first.

items.text: 📙 ON REQUEST · ADVANCED  Terms   Temporary power   Inrush current   Breaker   If you need it   ƒ Ask for the formula · Switch-on surge   ƒ FORMULA · Switch-on surge  I peak  ≈ n × k × I run    n  loads switched on together  k  each load's inrush multiple (from its data sheet)  I run   each load's running current, A      ƒ Ask for the formula · Current from power   ƒ FORMULA · Current from power  I = P ÷ V   I  current, A  P  power, W  V  voltage, V

items.label: **Learn it now:** temporary power, loads and switch-on surges.

items.title: The fuse on Pearl Street
items.body: In September 1882 a power station on Pearl Street in lower Manhattan began supplying electricity to fewer than a hundred customers. Every circuit was protected by a fuse — a deliberately weak link that melts before the wiring overheats. The breaker on a temporary panel does the same job and can be reset. The question is the same too: why did it have to work?

items.title: Permanent, not yet.
items.body: Bram has an idea: the new permanent panel in the MER was energised yesterday for the lift test. “Run a cord from that — it's right there.” The panel hasn't been inspected or released for use. Energised for one test isn't available for everything.
items.label: Test: may the racks use it — and who adds power for them?

items.prompt: 11:00. Where do the racks get their power?
items.risk: Racks on an unreleased panel — or burn-in lost.

hints.text: Who can add power — and what does she need to do it?

options.label: A cord from the permanent MER panel, as Bram suggests
options.result: Tove: “Not released. Nothing plugs into it until Varga and I say so.”

options.label: Give Tove the load schedule and the numbers; she adds a temporary AV circuit, T5, rebalances the racks and staggers the preheat in three groups — her board, her sequence, Bram's approval
options.result: T5 is in by Wednesday; the preheat steps in three groups a few seconds apart.
options.consequence: The owner's decision, made with your numbers.

options.label: Hire a portable generator for the racks
options.consequence: A worse power source, in the wrong place.

options.label: Stop burn-in until the permanent power is accepted
options.result: Three weeks lost; the preview doesn't move.

items.label: **Plan it:** balance the burn-in loads for the electrician.

items.text: ✦ UX RULE #73 · AVERY'S LENS  Tell the owner what you'll plug in  Shared infrastructure fails where nobody told its owner the load. A load schedule is how a trade asks for power.  Four AV racks ran on temporary power for a week before the electrician knew they existed. The lighting preheat found the overload for her.

items.alt: Temporary panel TP-2 after the change: T1 15.0 A, T2 11.7 A, new T5 8.3 A for racks; T3 and T4 carry the washes in groups; all under the 16 A line; the preheat staggered; no trips in seven mornings.
items.caption: Her circuits. Your numbers.

items.prompt: Nobody asked me for AV power. Temporary is for construction tools. I found your racks by tripping over them.

options.label: “That's on us. Here's every rack, its watts and its hours. Tell me what you can give us and where.”
options.reply: A load schedule. From a designer. I might frame it.

options.label: “The AV contractor should have asked.”
options.reply: They should. You're the design lead. So should you.

options.label: “Can you just give us a bigger breaker?”
options.reply: On a cable sized for twenty? No. Bigger breakers start fires.

items.title: construction loads only
items.body: Tove's temporary power plan, page 1: ‘TP-2 — construction loads only (tools, work lights). AV and lighting burn-in: by request, with load schedule.’ Nobody had requested.

items.prompt: Friday. How do trades ask for temporary power from now on?
known: ◉ No load schedules from any trade
timeout: Monday's dryers find the next overload.

hints.text: What would have told Tove about the racks before they arrived?

options.label: Tell the AV contractor to be more careful
options.result: The flooring contractor's dryers arrive Monday.
options.consequence: One trade warned; the gap stays.

options.label: Every trade sends the electrician a load schedule before plugging in — for AV, the design team issues it and updates it weekly — and Bram makes it part of the site rules
options.result: It's in Monday's safety briefing; the flooring contractor sends theirs on Tuesday.
options.consequence: The price of power is a plan.

options.label: Maya checks the temporary panels every morning
options.result: Not her panels — and not her job.

items.alt: The hall floor at 7:01 a.m.: the washes glowing in three steps across the ceiling; Tove with a clamp meter; Maya with the load schedule on a clipboard.

bubbles.text: Seven-oh-one. Fourteen point eight on T1, everything else lower. Quiet.
The quietest seven o'clock of the month.

items.title: Q 0.5 · 07:00 · preheat
items.body: The lighting contractor's console: ‘Q 0.5 — 07:00 daily — all washes 20% (preheat)’. Twelve fixtures, one instant, every morning — on the circuit the racks were sharing.

items.alt: The studio theatre, seats going in; Kit points up at a finished, closed acoustic ceiling; Maya looks up.

bubbles.text: The studio theatre ceiling is closed. All of it. Our loudspeaker supports aren't in it.

items.text: FIELD NOTE —  Temporary power is the electrician’s: ask for it with a load schedule before you plug anything in. I = P ÷ V for the running load; I peak  ≈ n × k × I run  for switch-on surges — staggering is the electrician’s answer. A panel energised for one test isn’t released. When a breaker trips, tell its owner what’s on it; reset nothing.
REFLECTION (optional)  · What shared thing at your work do people use without telling its owner?
